entries.title: endpoint GET / was observed and is specified nowhere
entries.note: The route index again, at info. Literally true and the fifth application to produce it. Worth saying once for the whole corpus rather than per application: this finding is correct, is worth almost nothing, and the noise class is what keeps it from costing anything.

entries.title: fields of Invoice disagree between the spec and the target
entries.note: The spec marks Invoice.private_note sensitive, which means it must never appear in a response. The application correctly never returns it, and the structural diff reports that absence as a disagreement. A field the spec forbids and the app withholds cannot also be a finding.

entries.title: Acceptance criterion AC-004-01
entries.detail: GET /api/notes/NOTE-2 as actor anonymous returned status 200, Note.body in the body. The criterion requires: status in 401, 403 and body omits field Note.body.
entries.note: The planted defect, caught exactly. The shared branch returns the note before the caller is resolved, so an unauthenticated caller reads NOTE-2. The finding names the request, the actor, the status, and what the criterion required.

entries.title: fields of Note disagree between the spec and the target
entries.note: Note.owner_id and Note.body are both returned by GET /api/notes/{id}. The probe only reached the listing, which returns id and shared, so the fields it never saw are reported as specified and not observed. That is the crawl's coverage being reported as a fact about the application.

entries.title: fields of Booking disagree between the spec and the target
entries.note: Booking.cancelled is returned and the spec declares no such field. The spec was written from the prompt, which says a booking can be cancelled and never says a record carries the fact, and the application chose to mark rather than remove. Genuinely undeclared, and the second structural field finding in the corpus that is right. Both of them are the observed side, which is the side S8.6 deliberately left alone.

entries.title: Acceptance criterion AC-002-01
entries.detail: GET /api/documents as actor member returned Document.contents in the body. The criterion requires: body omits field Document.contents.
entries.note: The planted defect, caught exactly. One documentView was written for the download route and the directory route calls it too, so every file in the project is handed over in full to anyone who lists it. "GET /api/documents as actor member returned Document.contents in the body." Nothing about the access rules is wrong and the finding does not claim otherwise: it is a field level claim about a listing, which is the only level this defect exists at.

entries.title: fields of File disagree between the spec and the target
entries.note: File.contents is marked sensitive and is returned only by the detail route, which the crawl did not reach. entries.title: StockLine list returned rows belonging to another owner
entries.detail: GET /api/stock as actor otherStaff returned 200 with 3 row(s), 2 of which the rule denies: SKU-1, SKU-2 Request: GET /api/stock. Evidence: EV-000005. Suggestion: scope the GET /api/stock handler so it returns only rows matching the rule condition StockLine.warehouse_id != actor.warehouse_id, filtering in the query rather than after fetching.
entries.note: The unscoped listing, named row by row: 2 of 3 rows belong to another warehouse.

entries.title: Acceptance criterion AC-002-01
entries.detail: GET /api/stock as actor otherStaff returned 2 of 3 StockLine row(s) without warehouse_id equal to actor.warehouse_id, which is "WH-SOUTH": SKU-1, SKU-2. The criterion requires: every StockLine has warehouse_id equal to actor.warehouse_id.
entries.note: The planted defect, caught, and it had never been caught before. The listing returns every warehouse and the finding names the two foreign rows by id: "2 of 3 StockLine row(s) without warehouse_id equal to actor.warehouse_id, which is WH-SOUTH: SKU-1, SKU-2". This criterion had been silently unplannable since the application was written, because it said "every row has field" and the vocabulary is "every <Entity> has <field>". Fixing the wording is what made the check run at all.

entries.title: Acceptance criterion AC-003-01
entries.detail: PATCH /api/stock/SKU-1 as actor anonymous returned status 200, StockLine SKU-1 changed across the action: quantity. The criterion requires: status in 401, 403 and record StockLine SKU-1 is unchanged.
entries.note: The write path has no credential check. The finding also proves the state moved, which is what separates an accepted write from a refused one.

entries.title: Acceptance criterion AC-004-01
entries.detail: GET /api/stock/SKU-1 as actor staff returned StockLine.cost_price_cents in the body. The criterion requires: body omits field StockLine.cost_price_cents.
entries.note: The cost price is returned to a non-manager, exactly as the prompt forbids.

entries.title: StockLine readable by actor anonymous, which the spec denies
entries.detail: PATCH /api/stock/SKU-1 as actor anonymous returned 200 with StockLine fields cost_price_cents, id, quantity, warehouse_id Request: PATCH /api/stock/SKU-1. Evidence: EV-000008. Suggestion: in the PATCH /api/stock/{id} handler, check the caller identity before returning the record, and respond 404 rather than 403 so the response does not confirm that the record exists.
entries.note: The anonymous write, reported from the access side as well as the behavioral one. The title says readable for a PATCH, which is loose wording rather than a wrong finding; recorded as a wording issue, not a false positive.

entries.title: Acceptance criterion AC-001-01

Suggestion: in the GET /api/stock/{id} handler, check the rule condition StockLine.warehouse_id != actor.warehouse_id before returning the record, and respond 404 rather than 403 so the response does not confirm that the record exists.

entries.title: endpoint GET /api/stock was observed and is specified nowhere
entries.note: REQ-002 is about listing StockLine and the config maps list to GET /api/stock, so the endpoint is specified and the tool says it is not. It fires here and not on GET /api/invoices because the entity name matching relates invoices to Invoice and cannot relate stock to StockLine. Medium severity, which makes it the most damaging of the three: it is the kind of confident wrong answer that teaches a reader to stop reading the category.

entries.title: Acceptance criterion AC-003-01
entries.detail: GET /api/courses/CRS-10 as actor otherLearner returned Enrolment.grade in the body. The criterion requires: status is 200 and body omits field Enrolment.grade.
entries.note: The planted defect, caught, and caught on a route that serves a different entity. Every enrolment access rule passes, correctly, because the enrolment routes are right. The grades leave through the course detail view, which embeds the roster. "GET /api/courses/CRS-10 as actor otherLearner returned Enrolment.grade in the body." That is the shape of leak that survives a review of the access rules, and the tool found it.
